content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted. Per our Spec-Driven workflow, **this is a review gate** — nothing gets planned or built until you approve the spec.

## 📄 Specification: Bookmark Manager
`specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` — all quality checks pass.

### What the app does (in scope for v1)
| Priority | User story |
|----------|-----------|
| **P1** | **Save a bookmark** — enter a URL, optional title & tags; it appears in the list |
| **P2** | **Browse & search** — find links by keyword across title, address, and tags |
| **P3** | **Edit & delete** — correct titles/tags, remove with confirmation |
| **P3** | **Organize with tags** — filter the list down to one tag |

### Key requirements
- Validates web addresses; derives a title when none is given
- Opens destinations in a new tab
- Live search as you type; clear empty states
- **Persists** bookmarks across close/reopen
- Warns on duplicate URLs

### Success criteria (measurable)
- Save a bookmark in under 20s; find one among 100+ in under 5s
- Search/filter responds within 1s up to 1,000 bookmarks
- 100% persistence across restarts

### Notable scope boundaries (in Assumptions)
- **Single user, one device; no login** in v1
- **No sync, no browser import/export** in v1
- Browser-based web app; no page-preview fetching or link-liveness checks

---

Please review. A few decisions worth your confirmation before we plan:

1. **Single-user / no login for v1** — acceptable, or do you want accounts?
2. **No sync / no import-export in v1** — okay to defer?
3. Any must-have I've missed (e.g. favorites/pinning, folders vs. tags, notes on a bookmark)?

If it looks good as-is, say **approve** and I'll move to the planning gate (`speckit-plan`). If anything's off, tell me and I'll revise the spec — we route changes through the spec, not through code.

Single-user with no login is fine, and cross-device sync can wait. I don’t approve the specification yet, though—it leaves out several important parts of how I want to manage a growing collection.

Please revise it so that:

- Saving a link automatically picks up its title, description, site icon, and preview image, while still letting me edit the title and description.
- Saving the same address takes me to the existing bookmark to update it; it must not allow a second copy.
- A bookmark can have an editable address, description, and note as well as its title and tags.
- Existing tags are suggested while I type.
- Search covers titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses, ignores letter case, supports `#tag`, exact phrases, and combinations such as AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- I can mark links for reading later, see that list separately, and mark them read.
- I can archive links without deleting them, browse the archive separately, and restore them.
- I can select multiple links—or all links matching my current search or filter—and tag, archive, mark read/unread, or delete them together.
- I can sort the list, and each item clearly shows its title, description, tags, and site icon.
- I can save useful combinations of searches and included or excluded tags for reuse.
- I can import and export standard browser bookmark files, so please don’t defer that.
- I can preserve a local copy of a page, with PDFs saved as PDFs, and optionally preserve it through the Internet Archive.
- I can adjust basic display preferences such as the default sorting, number of items shown, and text size.

Notes should support simple formatting when displayed. Once these behaviours and their important edge cases are included, I can review the revised specification.

## 📄 Revised Specification: Bookmark Manager
`specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md` — all quality checks pass. Every behaviour you listed is now covered as a testable user story with acceptance scenarios, plus edge cases.

### What changed since the last draft

| Area | Now in the spec |
|------|-----------------|
| **Auto metadata** (P1) | Fetches title, description, site icon, preview image on save; title & description stay editable; graceful fallback + retry if fetch fails |
| **No duplicates** (P1) | Saving an existing address opens the existing bookmark to update — never a second copy; same rule on edit and import |
| **Richer bookmark** (P1) | Editable address, title, tags, description, and **note with simple formatting**; existing tags suggested as you type |
| **Advanced search** (P2) | Case-insensitive across title/description/note/address; `#tag`, `"exact phrases"`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, parentheses; clear errors on malformed queries |
| **Read-later** (P2) | Separate list; mark read/unread (read state tracked independently) |
| **Archive** (P2) | Archive without deleting, browse archive separately, restore, permanent delete |
| **Bulk actions** (P2) | Select items or "all matching current search/filter" → tag, archive, read/unread, delete together |
| **Sort & display** (P2) | Sort by date added / title / last updated; each item shows title, description, tags, site icon |
| **Saved searches** (P3) | Named query + included/excluded tags, reusable/renamable/deletable |
| **Import / export** (P2) | Standard browser bookmark files (folders→tags), with added/skipped/failed summary — **not deferred** |
| **Page preservation** (P3) | Local copy (PDFs saved as PDFs) + optional Internet Archive snapshot; graceful failure |
| **Display preferences** (P3) | Default sort, items shown, text size; persist across sessions |

### A few things I decided as defaults — please confirm or correct (recorded in **Assumptions**):

1. **Deduplication normalization**: I treat addresses as the same after lower-casing the host, dropping default ports, trailing slash, and common tracking params (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`). Different paths/real query params stay distinct. Reasonable?
2. **Search precedence**: `NOT` > `AND` > `OR`, parentheses override; unquoted multi-word = ANDed keywords. Match your expectation?
3. **Note formatting**: lightweight markdown-style (bold, italic, lists, links, headings) rendered safely — not full HTML. OK?
4. **Import/export format**: the standard Netscape bookmark HTML file used by major browsers. OK?
5. A **server-side component** is anticipated (metadata fetch, preservation, import/export can't be done from a browser page alone). The actual tech choice is deferred to the plan gate.

---

If this captures what you want, say **approve** and I'll move to the planning gate (`speckit-plan`). Otherwise tell me what to adjust and I'll revise the spec.

Also note: the Internet Archive and metadata fetching depend on outbound network access, which may be restricted in the review environment — the spec requires these to degrade gracefully.

The overall direction is right, but I’d like a few corrections before approving:

- For duplicate detection, lower-casing the site name and ignoring a default port are fine. Please don’t automatically remove tracking parameters or trailing slashes, since those can sometimes lead to genuinely different pages. Only treat addresses as duplicates when they are safely equivalent.
- The search order of operations is fine. Please also specify that words such as “AND,” “OR,” and “NOT” can be searched literally by putting them in quotes.
- The note formatting approach is fine.
- The standard browser bookmark HTML format is fine. Importing must preserve each bookmark’s title, tags, and original date-added information where the file contains them.
- The server-side component is fine.
- A preserved web page should be stored as a self-contained HTML file representing the original page, not merely an extracted readable version. PDFs should continue to be stored as PDFs.
- Please ensure two tags with the same name cannot be created for this collection.

Once those points are reflected clearly, I expect the specification will be ready for approval.

All six corrections are now reflected in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`. We're still at the **spec review gate**.

## Corrections applied

1. **Deduplication — narrowed to safely-equivalent only** (US2 scenario 2, FR-007, Assumptions): normalization is now limited to lower-casing the host and ignoring a default port. **Trailing slashes and query/tracking parameters are kept distinct**, since they can point to genuinely different pages.

2. **Literal AND/OR/NOT in search** (US4 new scenario 5, FR-012): putting `"AND"`, `"OR"`, `"NOT"` (or a phrase containing them) in quotes searches them as literal text instead of operators. Precedence (`NOT`>`AND`>`OR`, parens override) unchanged.

3. **Note formatting** — unchanged, as you confirmed.

4. **Import preserves title, tags, and original date-added** where present in the file (US10 scenario 1, FR-026), on top of the Netscape HTML format and folder→tag mapping.

5. **Preserved web page = self-contained HTML** representing the original page (embedding needed resources), *not* an extracted readable version; **PDFs still stored as PDFs** (US11 scenario 1, FR-029, edge cases, Assumptions, Preserved Copy entity).

6. **Unique tag names** (new FR-010a, Tag entity, US3 new scenario 5): a name that already exists (case-insensitive) reuses the existing tag — two tags with the same name can never be created.

Branch: `001-bookmark-manager` · Plan: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`

**Artifacts generated:**
- `plan.md` — approach, tech context, project structure

- `contracts/api.md` — the JSON API contract

### Proposed approach (plain terms)
A **single web app**: one Node.js server that both hosts the JSON API and serves a React interface, running on port 4000 as the review environment requires — one `npm start`, no second server.

| Concern | Choice | Why |
|---------|--------|-----|
| **Storage** | Local SQLite file + full-text index | Perfect for single-user local persistence; fast search to 5,000+ bookmarks |
| **Auto metadata & page preservation** | The environment's bundled Playwright + Chromium | Reliably reads JS-rendered metadata; captures a faithful **self-contained HTML** file (your requirement, not a readable extract); saves PDFs as PDFs |
| **Internet Archive** | Public "Save Page Now" endpoint, store snapshot reference | Meets the requirement without hosting archive infra; fails gracefully |
| **Search** | Custom boolean parser over the text index | Only robust way to honor `#tag`, phrases, AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, **and quoted-literal operators** |
| **Deduplication** | Canonical key = lowercased host + drop default port only | Exactly your narrowed rule — trailing slash / query / tracking params stay distinct; uniqueness enforced in the database |
| **Import/export** | Netscape bookmark HTML | Standard browser format; preserves title, tags (folders→tags), and original date-added |
| **Notes** | Markdown stored, sanitized & rendered | "Simple formatting," safely |
| **Frontend** | React built with Vite to static files | Handles live search, tag autocomplete, multi-select bulk bar cleanly |

### Notable points worth your eye
- **One process on port 4000** serving both API and UI (matches the presentation environment; avoids a second port).
- **Data lives under `/work/data/`** (SQLite + preserved page files), persisting across restarts.
- External features (metadata, preservation, Internet Archive) **degrade gracefully** when the network is restricted in the review container — you'll see honest status, not silent failure.
- All dependencies are mainstream; Playwright will be pinned to **1.61.0** to match the installed Chromium (per environment rules).

---

Does this approach look right? A couple of choices you may want to confirm:
1. **SQLite + local files** for storage (vs. anything heavier) — good for a single-user app?
2. **React/Vite** front end — acceptable, or do you prefer something simpler/server-rendered?

Reply **approve** and I'll proceed to the task breakdown gate (`speckit-tasks`). If you'd like any change, tell me and I'll revise the plan before we go further.

The correction is complete and running. This was a fidelity fix — the spec and plan were already correct, so I only changed the implementation to match them.

## Correction applied: pre-save review/edit step

**Before:** the save area took a URL and immediately created the bookmark.

**Now** — a two-step flow matching US1 (*"review and edit the automatically collected title and description before saving"*):

1. **Paste a URL → "Fetch details"** — the app fetches the title, description, site icon, and preview image but **does not save yet** (verified: bookmark count stayed unchanged after preview).
2. **Review panel** appears pre-filled with the collected title and description (plus the preview image and an optional tags field). You can edit them, then **Save bookmark** — or **Cancel**. Verified: an edited title/description was saved exactly as entered.
3. If the URL is already saved, the fetch step recognizes the duplicate and opens the **existing** bookmark to edit instead — no second copy.

Editing title/description **after** saving still works through the edit dialog, as before.

### How it was done
- New `POST /api/bookmarks/preview` fetches metadata (or reports a duplicate) **without** creating a row.
- `POST /api/bookmarks` now reuses the already-fetched metadata so the page isn't fetched twice.
- The client's add area became a fetch → review/edit → save panel (`client/src/App.jsx`); metadata failures fall back to manual entry.
